doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Reverend Turner builds a homemade bass violin
summary: Turner spends two years building a bass from veneer and tacks, and Ware learns to play it in church with a few chords.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: And later, oh, maybe the middle thirties -- about '33 or '34, Reverend Turner decided to make a bass violin and he went out and got some veneer wood, some tacks and glue, and it took him a good 2 years to build that instrument, and he bought strings. The only thing, really, he had to buy were the strings and a bridge.

But it had a sound, [it was] sturdy -- and I got away from playing the drums in church and started the fiddle. He took me to church one night with him and said "You're gonna play it tonight." And him being the pastor, him sitting up in the pulpit, he showed me a few changes -- I played G, D, and C -- church songs, mostly.

And he tuned the fiddle up, like you tune a fiddle; with G, D, A and E. And if it rained, he had wooden pegs up there where he would have to twist them with his hand and take a hammer and tack it in to hold it, you know, because they would slip. The weather would get bad and the strings would stretch, and I just learned how to play across the fiddle that way. That was about the middle Thirties.
